assertions.summary: Both controllers report successful bidirectional replication for the domain, configuration, schema, DomainDnsZones, and ForestDnsZones naming contexts; DNS answers are available through both controllers.

evidence.command:
sudo -n samba-tool drs showrepl 2>&1
sudo -n samba-tool dbcheck --cross-ncs --quiet 2>&1
for server in dc1.corp.example dc2.corp.example
do
  dig +time=2 +tries=1 @"$server" corp.example SOA +short
  dig +time=2 +tries=1 @"$server" _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.corp.example SRV +short
  dig +time=2 +tries=1 @"$server" _kerberos._tcp.corp.example SRV +short
done
evidence.observation: Inbound neighbors from DC2 for all required naming contexts show successful last attempts and 0 consecutive failures. dbcheck exits 0 with no reported errors. Queries to both controller names return SOA data and both LDAP/Kerberos SRV targets.

evidence.command:

assertions.summary: Node1 has a complete validated SYSVOL; node2 lacks the Policies tree and fails SYSVOL ACL validation.

evidence.command:
sudo -n samba-tool ntacl sysvolcheck 2>&1
sudo -n find /var/lib/samba/sysvol/corp.example -maxdepth 3 -type d -print 2>&1 | sort
evidence.observation: sysvolcheck_rc=0. SYSVOL contains Policies with both required policy GUID trees and MACHINE/USER subtrees, plus scripts.

evidence.command:
sudo -n samba-tool ntacl sysvolcheck 2>&1
sudo -n find /var/lib/samba/sysvol/corp.example -maxdepth 3 -type d -print 2>&1 | sort
sudo -n stat -c '%A %U:%G %n' /var/lib/samba/sysvol /var/lib/samba/sysvol/corp.example /var/lib/samba/sysvol/corp.example/Policies /var/lib/samba/sysvol/corp.example/scripts 2>&1
evidence.observation: sysvolcheck returns 255 with No data available for /var/lib/samba/sysvol/corp.example. The tree contains only the realm directory and scripts; Policies is absent.

failures: Node2 has an incomplete SYSVOL: the required Policies tree is missing and samba-tool ntacl sysvolcheck fails with rc=255.
limitations: The node1 ACL-summary subcommand also reported getfacl not found, but samba-tool ntacl sysvolcheck independently returned rc=0.

evidence.observation: The engineering group exists and contains CN=infrasetuser,CN=Users,DC=corp,DC=example; group listmembers returns infrasetuser. The user exists with memberOf engineering, and winbind resolves both identities.

evidence.command:

sudo -n samba-tool dbcheck --cross-ncs --quiet 2>&1
evidence.observation: The controller reports successful replication of the domain naming context from DC2 with 0 consecutive failures and dbcheck exit 0, supporting convergence of the node2 identity state.

limitations: The direct node1 ldbsearch attempt was unavailable because ldbsearch is not installed; bidirectional NC replication, dbcheck, and node2's authenticated local AD object output supplied the convergence evidence.

assertions.summary: The canonical server identity and Kerberos ticketing are valid, but smbclient cannot establish the required Kerberos SMB session, so share read and evaluator file I/O do not complete.

evidence.command:
hostname -f
sudo -n testparm -s 2>&1
canonical=$(hostname -f)
for server in dc1.corp.example dc2.corp.example
do
  dig +time=2 +tries=1 @"$server" "$canonical" A +short
done
sudo -n net ads status -P 2>&1
sudo -n net ads keytab list 2>&1
evidence.observation: The implementation-defined canonical name is fileserver.corp.example. It resolves through both controllers, is the machine account dNSHostName, and the effective share path is /srv/corp/engineering. AD status lists the corresponding HOST principals; node4 later obtains kvno 1 for cifs/fileserver.corp.example@CORP.EXAMPLE.

evidence.command:
sudo -n stat -c '%A %a %U:%G %u:%g %n' /srv/corp/engineering /srv/corp/engineering/welcome.txt 2>&1
sudo -n sed -n '1,5p' /srv/corp/engineering/welcome.txt 2>&1
sudo -n wbinfo --group-info=engineering 2>&1
sudo -n getent group 'CORP\engineering' 2>&1
evidence.observation: The backing directory is setgid 2775 root:engineering, welcome.txt is 664 root:engineering, and its content is exactly infraset-samba. Effective share configuration allows CORP Domain Users and places CORP engineering in write list.

evidence.command:
sudo -n -H sh -c '. /root/corp-user.env
printf "%s\n" "$SAMBA_PASSWORD" | kinit "$principal"
kvno cifs/fileserver.corp.example@CORP.EXAMPLE'
evidence.observation: The declared SAMBA_USER and SAMBA_PASSWORD variables are present; kinit succeeds for infrasetuser@CORP.EXAMPLE; the Kerberos TGT is present and kvno for cifs/fileserver.corp.example@CORP.EXAMPLE succeeds with kvno 1.

evidence.command:
for server in dc1.corp.example dc2.corp.example
do
  dig +time=2 +tries=1 @"$server" fileserver.corp.example A +short
  dig +time=2 +tries=1 @"$server" corp.example SOA +short
  dig +time=2 +tries=1 @"$server" _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.corp.example SRV +short
  dig +time=2 +tries=1 @"$server" _kerberos._tcp.corp.example SRV +short
done
getent hosts fileserver.corp.example
nc -zvw2 fileserver.corp.example 445 2>&1
evidence.observation: Both controller DNS endpoints resolve the canonical fileserver name, return the CORP.EXAMPLE SOA and LDAP/Kerberos SRV records, and normal resolution succeeds. TCP/445 on fileserver.corp.example is open.

evidence.command:
smbclient --use-kerberos=required --use-krb5-ccache=/tmp/codex-samba-p2-node4.1XPdtw --no-pass -U "$principal" //fileserver.corp.example/engineering -c "get welcome.txt -" 2>&1
smbclient --use-kerberos=required --use-krb5-ccache=/tmp/krb5cc_0 --no-pass -U "$principal" //fileserver.corp.example/engineering -c "get welcome.txt -" 2>&1
evidence.observation: Both custom-cache and default-cache Kerberos smbclient attempts fail with gensec_gse_client_prepare_ccache: No password for user principal, Could not find a suitable mechtype, and NT_STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER. The evaluator create/modify/read/remove sequence was not attempted.

evidence.command:
sudo -n find /srv/corp/engineering -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -printf '%M %u:%g %p\n' 2>&1 | sort
sudo -n smbstatus --brief 2>&1
evidence.observation: After the failed SMB attempts, only the declared welcome.txt remains and there are no active SMB sessions; no evaluator file was created.

failures: The executor's installed smbclient cannot complete required Kerberos SMB session setup against the validated canonical endpoint, so welcome.txt cannot be read through SMB and evaluator file I/O cannot be completed.
Because no SMB evaluator file was created, post-I/O ownership evidence is unavailable.
limitations: The custom-cache and authorized default-cache retry both failed at SMB GSSAPI session setup; this is treated as a live share-access failure, not as missing DNS or Kerberos-ticket evidence.

Executed all eight Probe 2 evidence checks, including canonical CIFS discovery, DNS validation, Kerberos ticket acquisition, and SMB access attempts.
Executed the two reserved Probe 2 cleanup calls; removed evaluator custom/default Kerberos caches and temporary paths, with no evaluator share file present.

overall_summary: Roles, joins, current bidirectional AD/DNS replication, required identities, and the declared share configuration pass. Node2 SYSVOL health fails. The canonical CIFS name and Kerberos tickets validate, but smbclient Kerberos session setup fails, so SMB share access and evaluator file I/O fail. Operational cleanliness also fails because enabled ssh.service is failed on all four nodes and stale winbind cache backups remain on node3 and node4. No outage, recovery, or reboot persistence test was authorized.
